title: Managed versus native OpenVDB cached access
scope: Two local coherent cached-access kernels on an existing UInt16 Tree4 5/4/3, Windows x64. No library optimization. Final result: E2 on logical CPU 16; the more heavily contended E1 on CPU 8 remains in epochs/E1.
question: How do matching managed and native cached reads/writes compare on the same warmed coordinate stream?
primaryMetric: milliseconds per operation; median of launch medians

summary.headline: Read managed/native time ratio 2.153x; write 2.863x. Ratios describe these kernels, not general OpenVDB performance.

correctness: Native/managed UInt16 Tree4 5/4/3 fixture: identical coordinate hashes, 32768 active voxels, 64 leaves, checksum 147456.
Every measured read sum checked against count/8 × 36; every write pass changes the value phase and validates all 32768 values/activity outside timing.
Both restore the initial state before each workload and after measurements.
validityThreats: A warm 32×32×32 coordinate working set with 87.5% leaf-cache hit rate; not random access, cold data, tree creation, meshing, filtering or I/O.
Different implementation languages, compilers, layouts and accessor cache levels; the result cannot identify a single causal mechanism.
No application-level speedup, universal performance advantage, confidence interval or native allocation measurement is claimed.
Shared host lock is cooperative. External applications can still affect CPU/cache/power; per-CPU load snapshots are recorded in raw/environment.json.
Allocation counters cover the managed current thread only. Native memory allocation is not instrumented.
Default safe native accessor versus managed structural-version invalidation; both conform for this no-topology-change workload.
Native dependency build paths contain prior reference artifacts; exact static-library SHA-256, source revision and compiler settings are retained.
Native write launch medians in E2 vary from 0.00000440416 to 0.00000587976 ms/op. Background load and frequency drift remain; use approximate ratios rather than a precise guarantee.
reproduction: Run the driver through scientific-method-performance/scripts/run_with_performance_lock.py; see benchmarks/CACHED_COMPARISON.md.
Use the pinned native checkout and Release reference libraries. All disposable builds/dependencies go under the named D:\Workspaces\AI task directory.
